messages:
customer-james: Hey team, intermittent 502s from our private Redwood endpoint behind an NLB since last night. App shows unhealthy targets. No config changes on our side. Help?

alex: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick Q: is this Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment?

customer-james: Private (VPC). We have egress allowlist on our firewall/NAT. The app's /ready endpoint calls an internal auth service (10.10.20.5) and also does a DNS lookup for mgmt.redwood.local. Health checks just started failing after a firewall rule cleanup yesterday.

maria: That sounds like egress-related. NLB health checks hit the instance IP directly; if the readiness handler does outbound DNS or TLS calls, blocked egress could make it return 500/timeout which marks the target unhealthy. Can you paste the pod/instance logs around the probe time?

customer-james: Here's a trimmed snippet from the app logs when probe hits:

```
2026-03-16T22:11:05Z GET /health/ready 200 start
2026-03-16T22:11:05Z calling auth service at http://10.10.20.5/ok
2026-03-16T22:11:05Z dns lookup mgmt.redwood.local -> NXDOMAIN
2026-03-16T22:11:07Z auth call failed: connect ETIMEDOUT
2026-03-16T22:11:07Z /health/ready 502
```

samir: Thanks. Two possible issues: (1) DNS for mgmt.redwood.local failing because internal DNS forwarders are blocked, (2) egress rules preventing calls to the auth service or outbound CA CRL/OCSP. Which firewall rules were removed?

customer-james: We removed broad allow for 52.95.0.0/16 during the cleanup and replaced with a smaller set. I suspect some Redwood infra IPs are in that range.

alex: Are you using NAT Gateway egress or a managed egress appliance? Also, does the app try to reach any public AWS IPs for certificate revocation (OCSP) or an internal ops endpoint?

customer-james: NAT Gateway in a public subnet. We had an allowlist for specific external IPs only. The app's TLS stack tries OCSP to ocsp.redwood-infra.net (public) during startup. Could that be the root cause?

maria: Yes — if your readiness probe performs TLS handshakes that trigger OCSP fetching and the NAT egress is blocked to ocsp.redwood-infra.net IPs, the probe could hang until timeout. Also some Envoy sidecars make admin calls out. Next steps: can you tcpdump on the instance during a failing probe window to see what outbound destinations are attempted?

customer-james: Ran a quick tcpdump. Extract below (IPs masked):

```
11:11:05.123456 IP 10.0.2.14.52344 > 10.10.20.5.80: Flags [S], seq 0
11:11:05.456789 IP 10.0.2.14.33456 > 203.0.113.45.80: Flags [S], seq 0  # OCSP
11:11:07.000000 IP 10.0.2.14 > 10.10.20.5: ICMP host unreachable
```

samir: That matches: outbound to 203.0.113.45 (OCSP) is attempted and auth call times out. The ICMP host unreachable suggests the firewall/NAT is dropping or rejecting. Can you temporarily allow egress to that OCSP IP and the auth service to validate?

customer-james: Will do. If we allow it, any other things to check? Health check path and LB config?

alex: Also double-check the target group's health check path, port, and expected response code. For NLB, TCP-level checks can avoid app-level readiness flakiness if your readiness does external calls. But be careful: switching to TCP only verifies connection, not app readiness.

maria: If you need no external calls during readiness, modify readiness probe to be more lightweight (local check) or mock/stub external calls. Short-term fix: add egress allow for ocsp.redwood-infra.net and 10.10.20.5. Long-term: move OCSP stapling into your TLS termination so backends don't perform OCSP lookups on probe.

customer-james: Allowed egress to the OCSP IP and added explicit route to auth service. After that targets turned healthy within 30s. NLB shows 5/5 healthy now.

infra-bot: Deploy notification: customer-james private cluster firewall rule updated (+egress ocsp.redwood-infra.net) by james@infra at 2026-03-16T22:15:03Z.

alex: Great — closing loop. We'll add a KB entry for "health checks failing due to egress allowlists / OCSP". @maria can you draft? :thumbsup:

maria: On it. Drafted notes and suggested mitigations: lightweight readiness probes, OCSP stapling, explicit egress allowlist entries (OCSP IP ranges + internal auth service), and verifying NAT/GW SNAT behavior. I'll post the KB link here once ready.

customer-james: Thanks everyone, saved our morning.

samir: Follow-up action: we should surface this in onboarding docs for Private deployments — note about external endpoints (OCSP, CRL) and how readiness probes may trigger egress.

customer-james: Agreed.
